Hi Ben —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our SIG and SOC 2 scoping we need a concise architecture overview showing how Redwood separates customer workloads for Dedicated and Private deployments, plus an explicit statement on:

- Network/tenant boundary (VPC routing, transit, VLANs)
- Egress controls and outbound filtering
- KMS boundary and key ownership for Private deployments
- How fallbacks (model variants/regions) are handled w.r.t. isolation

Joao —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide:

1) A one-page architecture summary describing Dedicated vs Private isolation models.
2) A network diagram showing VPC boundaries, transit (Direct Connect / VPN), and on-prem routing for Private deployments.
3) A KMS boundary statement describing customer-managed keys (Bring-Your-Own-KMS) options and proof points for encryption-in-flight and at-rest.

Attachments I will send in the next message: redwood-tenant-boundaries-20260802.pdf and network-diagram-vpc-onprem-20260802.png.

Proposed timeline: initial artifacts 48 hours, final evidence bundle (including signed statement) by EOD Friday if that works.

Joao —

Per my note earlier, attached are the initial artifacts:

Attachments:
- redwood-tenant-boundaries-20260802.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — explains segregation model for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, tenancy controls, and routing policy examples.
- network-diagram-vpc-onprem-20260802.png (PNG) — diagram showing VPC subnets, peering/Transit Gateway, dedicated GPU pools, and on-prem VPN/Direct Connect lanes.

Summary highlights from the PDF:
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools with tenant routing at the load balancer and network ACLs enforcing egress rules; shared control plane (metadata only) lives in a separate management VPC with strict peering rules.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer VPC/Direct Connect option or our appliance-based airgapped option; all traffic originating from customer workloads can be forced through customer-managed egress.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS + external HSM for Private; encryption keys never leave the customer's KMS and are referenced by our runtime using short-lived IAM roles.

If you want, Grace (solutions) and David (infrastructure) can join a 30-minute call to step through the diagram. If acceptable, we'll also add a signed KMS boundary statement to the final evidence bundle.

Ben
